newsitem.title: FRANCE: Protesters occupy French finance ministry hall.
newsitem.headline: Protesters occupy French finance ministry hall.

text.p: Several dozen people protesting against unemployment occupied an office at the entrance to the French Finance Ministry on Wednesday and demanded a hearing for their campaign against "economic terror".

The protesters, part of a group which stopped in Paris on a two-month march to Amsterdam, said they took over the building to press demands for a shorter work week to reduce joblessness and better financial help for those out of work.
The protest came as France's prepares for a two-round parliamentary election on May 25 and June 1.
A Finance Ministry official said the protesters arrived in the late afternoon and demanded to be allowed to send their message to President Jacques Chirac by fax.
"There's no problem. We can understand their worries but what we want is that all this happens in an orderly fashion," said the official.

Demonstrators against joblessness are marching to Amsterdam from cities across Europe and are due to reach the Dutch capital on the eve of a mid-June summit of European Union leaders. The group in Paris comprises marchers from several European countries.

The occupation was the second in a week by activists opposing French economic policy and European monetary union plans, saying they run roughshod over the poor and marginalised. Another group occupied offices of the Bank of France last week.
